messages:
Alex: quick flag — after the morning canary some dashboards are much slower for large orgs. p75 LCP up by ~600ms on the heavy dash routes. Can we triage?

deploy-bot: deploy started: canary/redwood-console@release-2026-03-20 (PR #842)

Tara: confirmed. CPU on client traces spikes when opening the heatmap. Flamegraphs show repeated full renders of ChartCanvas + layout thrash.

Jun: telemetry rolling 6h: client CPU for /dash/* +28%, sessions with >2s render x3, p75 LCP +620ms starting exactly at the canary timestamp.

Sasha: looked at PR #842 diff — two risky changes: memo key swap for chart layout and enabling aggressive route prefetch for nested dash children. Either could explain churn.

Mike: memo change was `useMemo(..., [series])` instead of using a stable key. That will break shallow-equals and cause new refs every render.

Alex: that would trigger computeLayout each state tick — matches flamegraph.

Sasha: repro steps locally: open dashboard, move time range, see layout recompute logs and long tasks. I have a minimal patch to restore primitive-based keying.

Sasha: patch snippet to revert memo key:
```
- const layout = useMemo(() => computeLayout(series), [series])
+ const layout = useMemo(() => computeLayout(series), [series.map(s => s.id).join('|')])
```

Tara: also observed that prefetch is adding `range` to prefetched URLs which invalidates our prefix-based cache. If prefetch races with interactive loads we get both cache misses and double work.

Mike: prefetch intent was to improve perceived latency, but priming the full timeseries payload is too heavy. We should limit prefetch to metadata or stub responses for now.

Jun: proposed short action list:
- revert memo key change (Sasha)
- change prefetch to metadata-only for nested dash routes (Mike)
- add temporary client-side prefetch concurrency cap and server-side quota (ops-oncall)
- canary telemetry gating and close monitoring (Jun)

ops-oncall: ack. I'll add a client circuit-breaker (cap concurrent prefetches to 3 per session) and a server quota endpoint 10rps/org for prefetch; will return 429 when hit.

Sasha: opened hotfix PR #854 with memo revert and a unit test asserting computeLayout not recomputed for stable series refs. Link: https://git.redwood.dev/r/redwood/console/pull/854

Alex: hotfix vs full rollback? Hotfix is quicker if tests pass.

Tara: prefer merging hotfix to canary then ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 25% if CPU improves. Rollback if not.

Jun: monitoring live. Adding a short-lived telemetry eval to track layout compute counts per session so we can validate quickly.

Mike: I'll remove data prefetch for heavy children routes in the router config and swap to a lazy 'Load chart' affordance for very large series. That reduces background load while still enabling quick interactive fetch.

deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: canary/redwood-console@hotfix-854

Jun: early canary numbers look promising — p75 LCP down ~340ms for the canary cohort and client CPU trending down. Continuing to observe for 30m.

ops-oncall: quota and circuit breaker in place. To test: `curl -H "X-Org: 123" https://canary.api.redwood/dash/prefetch?range=7d` should return 429 after the short quota.

Alex: great work. Keep updates here. If canary stays stable for 30m we'll promote. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
